notes.3e: (i) Candidates understood how to obtain this probability. There are fewer instances of candidates giving answers as ratios, the overwhelming majority of candidates giving the answer as a fraction (although not necessarily in its lowest form), a percentage or a decimal.

notes.3iii: Candidates were much better this year in understanding that if an event is impossible then the probability must be zero.

notes.key_messages:
To succeed in this paper candidates need to have completed full syllabus coverage, remember necessary
formulae, show all necessary working clearly and use a suitable level of accuracy.
notes.general_comments:
The paper gave the opportunity for candidates to demonstrate their knowledge and application of
mathematics. The majority of the candidates were able to use the allocated time to good effect and
complete the paper. It was noted that the majority of candidates answered all of the questions with some
omitting a question on a particular topic. The standard of presentation and amount of working shown was
generally good. In particular candidates showed improvement in their drawing of curves. Few instances of
joining points with straight lines were evident. There were still a few instances of candidates rubbing out
construction lines and/or working in questions losing them marks. Centres should continue to encourage
candidates to show clear working in the answer space provided; the formulae used, substitutions and
calculations performed are of particular value if an incorrect answer is given.
